raw_response:
Well, let me think through this season. I'm 64 now, been working this ground for 45 years, and these last couple of years it's just been me in the house. That changes how I farm — not what I grow, but how much I can do with my own hands.

My 19.1 mu is all wheat-maize, same as everyone around here. The wheat went in last October, about the 10th like always. Right now it's greening up, so I'm thinking about the spring work and then turning it around to maize in June.

**On the wheat:** I put down about 40 kg of 15-15-15 compound per mu before planting last fall — that's my usual base. Nothing fancy. The extension station tells us to do soil testing and split the nitrogen more carefully, I went to one of those trainings years ago, but on my land 13-14 kg of N per mu has always given me around 450 kg wheat. Why change. In about two weeks when it greens up proper, I'll do the first irrigation — that's the important one, washes the fertilizer down. Then at jointing I topdress 15 kg of urea per mu and irrigate again. If April-May is dry I'll do a third watering at heading, but each irrigation costs me nearly 40 yuan per mu with the electric pump, so I only do it if the ground is really dry. Herbicide for the grass weeds once in spring — the little-flower weed (播娘蒿) and wild oats are my worst ones. If aphids show up bad at heading, I spray, otherwise leave it.

**On the maize:** This is where being alone hurts. The turnaround from wheat harvest to maize planting is 3-5 days, no time to plow. I pay the combine man to harvest the wheat and chop the straw, then I call the no-till seeder — he drops seed and compound fertilizer in one pass. About 40 yuan/mu for the service but I can't do it myself anymore. I use a regular hybrid, Zhengdan or whatever the agri-shop is selling that year that the neighbors had luck with. Another 15 kg urea topdress at big-flare stage (大喇叭口). July rains usually cover the water, but if it's dry I irrigate once. Fall armyworm has been showing up the last few years so I keep some insecticide ready.

**What worries me:** Fertilizer prices are still high, and the electricity for the pump keeps creeping up. Labor is my real constraint — I hire machinery for everything heavy now (planting, harvest, deep tillage every few years). I don't take any risks with new varieties or new methods. At my age, a bad year is too hard to come back from.
